newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly lose ground again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly lose ground again.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices mostly moved lower again Monday in fairly quiet trade, with soft demand, ample avails and relatively cheap gas still undermining sentiment, industry sources said.
"The market doesn't feel very good. There's still a lot of oil in the Caribs and resid has to compete against gas," said a cash trader, adding less than six weeks of winter remained.

In New York Harbor, physical one percent eased slightly to $17.25-50 a barrel, with February one percent paper steady at $17.00-25 and March paper off a quarter to $16.75-17.00 despite firmer crude, traders said.

Traders said talk that some East Coast utilities had switched to gas continued to undermine low sulphur sentiment. NYH 0.3 percent high pour slipped 50 cents to $19.75-20, while low pour notionally was 75 cents lower at $20.75-21.00 on reports 60,000 barrels for Feb 20-28 delivery sold at $20.75 (delivered).

U.S. Gulf refinery problems continued to weigh on high sulphur though traders said a Citgo coker fire Friday in Louisiana was seen as a short-term outage with little impact. NYH 2.2 percent was down a quarter to the $15.50 area.
U.S. Gulf one percent eased slightly to $16.25, while three percent was 20 cents lower at $12.75.
New York city gate gas prices were steady to up slightly to the $2.90-95/mmBtu area. NYH one percent resid fell to a $2.76/mmBtu equivalent.
